title: Scroll fields
description: Components are interactive building blocks for creating a user interface. They can be organized into categories based on their purpose: Action, containment, communication, navigation, selection, and text input.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
• Two different modes of input: scroll and input

  • Three recommended sizes: small (1-2 digits), medium (3 digits), and large (4 digits)

  • Can be finite or an infinitely looping list

  • Can be combined to select different measurements and include multiple values

contentChunks.footer: Scroll fields come in three sizes: small, medium, and large
contentChunks.altText: 6 variations of the scroll field at varying widths.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Color

Color values are implemented through design tokens. For design, this means working with color values that correspond with tokens. For implementation, a color value will be a token that references a value. Learn more about design tokens

contentChunks.htmlValue: Measurements
Scroll fields hug the contents by default, down to a minimum width and height per size. In larger windows, the fields can fill the container instead, or have a custom fixed size.

contentChunks.footer:
1. Small (1-2 digits)

  2. Medium (3 digits)

  3. Large (4 digits)
contentChunks.altText: Diagram of width and height measurements for scroll fields, by number of digits.

contentChunks.htmlValue: High contrast
High contrast mode is an accessibility feature that aims to maximize legibility by using a limited color palette, like black and white. Learn more about high contrast

contentChunks.footer: Scroll field in high-contrast mode
contentChunks.altText: Two fields, one with scroll and one with direct input, using high-contrast mode.

contentChunks.footer: Scroll fields provide a flexible, focused way for people to input or adjust specific measurements and numeric values
contentChunks.altText: Close-up of a scroll field component selecting height.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Usage
Scroll fields are an expressive way to select from a list of options. They're best used for numbers, but can be customized to many different use cases.

contentChunks.footer: Scroll fields are best used for choosing from a list of numbers
contentChunks.altText: Fitness app with scroll fields used to set desired heart rate.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Scroll fields can be used for time selection, as well as other units of measurement like distance, weight, or temperature.

contentChunks.footer: Temperature can be set through paired scroll fields
contentChunks.altText: UI displaying scroll fields setting temperature.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Use scroll fields alongside other controls, like button groups, to set more specific filters or add greater choice.

If using scroll fields to choose time, use a time picker instead.

contentChunks.footer: Scroll fields can be used along with options for day to add precision
contentChunks.altText: Bottom sheet with an alarm using scroll fields for time, along with button group options for date of week.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Multiple scroll fields can be placed side by side. If each scroll field is tracking a different value, clearly label each field.

contentChunks.footer: Add labels to scroll fields affecting different values
contentChunks.altText: A timer with three scroll fields aligned to hours, minutes, and seconds.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Support keyboard input

For accessibility, scroll fields should have an option to swap to text input for keyboard users. Place this button near the scroll field.

In scroll time pickers, this button is built-in.

contentChunks.footer: When scroll fields are present, the keyboard icon allows switching to text input
contentChunks.altText: Fitness app displaying a field for calories through scroll, with a keyboard icon to switch to text input.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Behavior

Scrolling

To scroll between values in a field, swipe the field, or tap the inactive value above or below to navigate to it.

contentChunks.footer: Scroll through values by swiping or tapping the inactive values
contentChunks.altText: ISO values are listed on a camera app, with inactive values scrollable by swiping or selecting the values themselves.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Motion

Scrolled items snap to always be vertically centered. The active value is darker with an increased font size.

contentChunks.footer: The item in the center of the container snaps into place
contentChunks.altText: Month and day in separate scroll fields being used for date selection.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Input behavior

When text input is selected, the numeric or standard keyboard can be used to select values.

For strings, the selection should auto-complete based on the initial character entered.

Any errors should appear below the scroll fields, and should highlight the incorrect value.

contentChunks.footer: Choosing text input swaps the focused scroll field to a text field
contentChunks.altText: UI for logging water shows numeric values added by keyboard after first selecting keyboard icon.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Sizing

Material recommends only using up to four digits in scroll fields. However, more digits can still be added as needed. There are three size options with their own minimum widths:

  • Small (1-2 digits): 100dp

  • Medium (3 digits): 144dp

  • Large (4 digits): 186dp

contentChunks.footer:
1. Small (1-2 digits)

  2. Medium (3 digits)

  3. Large (4 digits)
contentChunks.altText: Three different sizes of scroll fields: small with 2 digits, medium with 3 digits, and large with 4 digits.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Avoid very long lists in scroll fields, such as consecutive numbers with five or more digits. Values should be quick to scroll to.

To avoid excessive scrolling time, add intervals between values, or use a different component for precise entry, like a text field.

contentChunks.footer: Using five or more digits implies a long scroll time, unless values aren’t consecutive
contentChunks.altText: A banking app set to transfer money with the dollar amount running to five digits on a scroll field.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Placement

Inline is preferred

Whenever possible, place scroll fields inline with content. When scroll fields are inline, people can easily see surrounding content.

contentChunks.footer: Inline scroll fields are ideal for multiple values that should be set together, like ISO, shutter speed, and aperture camera settings
contentChunks.altText: Camera app showing values for aperture and shutter speed above a scroll field to select ISO value.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Non-modal dialog

When scroll fields can’t be placed inline, use a popup container like a non-modal dialog.

contentChunks.footer: When space is limited, scroll fields can be placed in a non-modal dialog
contentChunks.altText: An option to select a “custom amount” produces 2 scroll fields as a non-modal dialog to select total amount in ounces or liters.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Modal dialog

Modal dialogs should be used rarely, when the UI is too cluttered for a non-modal dialog.

contentChunks.footer: Scroll fields can be placed in modals if needed
contentChunks.altText: A modal listing temperature settings through two scroll fields.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Adaptive design
On larger screens, consider increasing scroll field height and width to more comfortably fill the containers they’re placed within.

contentChunks.footer: A taller and wider scroll field better fits the larger layout
contentChunks.altText: Scroll fields adapt to smaller or larger device size, filling the space.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Customizations

Scroll fields can be customized to have a fixed size, or to adapt in size depending on the space they’re placed in. To preserve usability:

  • Visually crop inactive values to indicate that more values are available by scrolling

  • Corner radius shouldn't be less than 16dp

contentChunks.footer: Scroll fields are customizable to fit panes of any size
contentChunks.altText: Custom widths for a scroll field.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Use cases

People should be able to use assistive technology to:

  • Select or enter values and units of measurement

  • Enter measurement selection manually using input fields
Interaction & style

Include both swipe & text input options

Any scroll field needs a way to also input text with a keyboard, like a toggle button next to the scroll fields, or a separate text field.

Material's scroll time picker has a built-in button that toggles to an input time picker. Consider using a similar pattern.

contentChunks.footer: Scroll fields are always paired with an input toggle in time pickers to allow text input
contentChunks.altText: The keyboard toggle on a scroll field activates input mode and allows direct entry of liters.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Targets

Targets for inactive values need to maintain a minimum height of 48dp, which stretches outside the container by default.

contentChunks.footer: All inactive values present should have a minimum 48dp height
contentChunks.altText: Diagram showing scroll field’s tap targets.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Keyboard navigation

Keys

Actions

Tab

Focus lands on scroll field

Space or Enter

Activates the scroll field

Up / Down

Selects option above or below in scroll field’s list
